children: Jefferies initiated coverage of Liberty Media’s Formula One
tracking stock FWONK with a Buy rating and a $115 price target, citing the company’s premium sports assets, asset-light model, and potential for margin expansion.
New PT represents a 21% upside from the stock's last close.

Analysts Anthony Berni and team called FWONK a “high-quality media & consumer experiences business” and said the streamlined focus on F1 and MotoGP following the Liberty Live separation and MotoGP acquisition should improve execution and capital allocation.

and MotoGP as the most underappreciated opportunities. It estimates the new Apple TV U.S. deal could boost F1 media-rights revenue by about $55 million annually through 2030, with further potential if Apple expands into international rights.

Berni also sees a significant MotoGP monetization opportunity, noting that F1 generates roughly five times MotoGP’s media-rights revenue, six times its race-promotion revenue, and 10 times its sponsorship revenue despite having about twice the global fan base.
“We believe investors may be underestimating FWONK’s potential scale and long-term earnings power,” the analysts said.

Jefferies forecasts revenue rising from $4.73 billion in 2025 to $5.84 billion in 2028, while adjusted OIBDA margins expand from 23.8% to 27.2%. Net leverage is expected to fall below 1x by year-end 2028 from about 3.8x following the MotoGP acquisition.

title: Jefferies starts Formula One at Buy with $115 target, cites Apple TV, MotoGP
